item.title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to this. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Don't change the footage.

item.tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

answer_sheet.Music mood and vocals: Tense instrumental music, with no singing.
answer_sheet.Music level relative to speech: Clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks; every original word must remain easy to hear.
answer_sheet.Source footage, duration, and framing: Keep the entire attached 7-second cockpit clip, with unchanged visuals, timing, and framing.
answer_sheet.Speech and added text: Keep the original radio-call recording in sync. Do not replace it or add text.

must_haves: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.

turns.text: Could you add a tense instrumental bed to this cockpit clip, with no singing? I’m a little worried the music could overwhelm the radio chatter instead of supporting the tension. What I mean is, keep the entire attached 7-second clip exactly as it is visually, without changing the footage, timing, or framing. Keep the music clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks so every original word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Please keep the original radio-call recording in sync, without replacing it or adding any text. The instruments and musical style are your call.

dialog.agent:
Your concern calls for **audio ducking**: keeping the instrumental bed low, then lowering it further beneath every radio call—especially “Rook, you with me?”—while leaving the original recording in sync.

The connected tools can generate instrumental music, but they can’t mix it into your existing clip or duck it beneath the dialogue. I therefore can’t deliver that exact edit here without compromising your requirements.

I can generate a separate tense instrumental track for an editor to trim to 7 seconds and mix underneath the untouched clip. The music generator’s minimum is 15 seconds. Would you like that standalone track? No credits have been spent.
dialog.user: Yes, please generate the standalone tense instrumental track, with no singing; the instruments and style are your call. My main worry is still keeping every original radio-call word easy to hear when it’s mixed in, especially “Rook, you with me?” The entire 7-second cockpit clip should stay unchanged, with the original recording in sync.

turns.agent:
The music generation was refused because your Magic Hour account has **insufficient credits**. No track was created, and your original clip remains untouched.

A 15-second instrumental requires **15 credits**. Once those are available, I can retry the restrained synth-drone bed with muted bass pulses and no vocals.

The eventual mix will still need dialogue ducking to keep every radio word clear—especially “Rook, you with me?”—without changing the footage or original audio timing.

style.prompt: Tense, restrained minimal cinematic electronic instrumental underscore for a cockpit scene with important radio dialogue. Low sustained synth drones, soft muted bass pulses, sparse dark atmospheric textures. Understated tension from the opening; first seven seconds should work as a continuous dialogue bed. Sparse arrangement leaving ample space for speech; avoid prominent midrange melodies, bright high frequencies, sharp percussion, impacts, abrupt swells and dramatic volume peaks. Steady subdued dynamics, no climax. Music only: no voices, no singing, no choir, no spoken words, no radio effects or chatter.
